Record date: 2129-07-31
South Elizabeth Seychelles Hospital INTERNAL MEDICINE DEPARTMENT Location: 4923 Olivia Parkway Suite 217, Lake Jennabury
PATIENT: Lysander Fairfax Phone: 28451903 email:bradleymorgan@example.org DATE OF BIRTH: 1947-05-12 AGE: 80 years
FOLLOW-UP DATE: 07/31/29 FOLLOWED BY: Dr. Emily Carter
CHIEF COMPLAINT
Persistent shortness of breath, worsening cough, and lower extremity swelling.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. Lysander Fairfax returns for follow-up after one week on the modified treatment plan initiated during his previous visit. He reports that while he has adhered to the prescribed oral prednisone and increased furosemide regimen, he continues to experience significant respiratory challenges. The shortness of breath persists, especially with exertion, and he describes his cough as now producing a yellow-green sputum, which has increased in volume. He denies any fever but reports episodes of chills and night sweats, raising concerns for possible underlying infection.
Despite the increase in furosemide to 160 mg daily, Mr. Fairfax notes that his bilateral lower extremity edema has not improved significantly, and he continues to experience discomfort and mobility limitations. He expresses frustration with his sleep quality, which remains poor despite the cognitive-behavioral strategies employed.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
General - + fatigue, - weight gain, + chills, + night sweats. Pulmonary - + persistent shortness of breath, + worsening cough with yellow-green sputum, - hemoptysis. Cardiac - no chest pain or palpitations, + orthopnea, - paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Gastrointestinal - no nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Musculoskeletal - + joint pain, + persistent bilateral lower extremity edema. Neurological - no dizziness or headaches.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: - Blood Pressure: 148/88 mmHg - Heart Rate: 92 bpm - Respiratory Rate: 26 breaths/min - Oxygen Saturation: 85% on room air
General: The patient appears fatigued and is in moderate respiratory distress, with notable accessory muscle use.
HEENT: No nasal flaring, oropharynx clear.
Lungs: Diminished breath sounds bilaterally with a notable increase in wheezing; bilateral crackles are more pronounced in the lower lung fields.
Cardiac: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops.
Extremities: Persistent bilateral lower extremity edema with significant pitting, particularly in the calves.
ASSESSMENT
1. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease exacerbation with worsening respiratory status; concern for possible pneumonia given the change in sputum characteristics and new systemic symptoms. 2. Congestive heart failure with ongoing fluid overload; current furosemide regimen appears inadequate. 3. Insomnia with ineffective cognitive-behavioral strategies; further intervention required.
PLAN
1. Order a chest X-ray to assess for pneumonia or other pulmonary complications, given the patient's increased sputum production and systemic symptoms. 2. Initiate a course of oral antibiotics (levofloxacin 750 mg daily for 7 days) to address potential bacterial pneumonia. 3. Increase furosemide to 200 mg daily to enhance diuresis and manage persistent bilateral lower extremity edema. 4. Continue nebulized albuterol every 2 hours and nebulized budesonide every 6 hours. 5. Monitor potassium levels closely due to the increased furosemide and maintain spironolactone at 25 mg daily. 6. Reassess insomnia management; consider a trial of low-dose trazodone at bedtime in conjunction with continued cognitive-behavioral strategies. 7. Educate the patient on the importance of adherence to the new medication regimen and recognition of signs of worsening infection or heart failure.
Mr. Fairfax verbalized understanding of the updated treatment plan and expressed a commitment to follow the new regimen.
DISPOSITION
Mr. Fairfax was stable for discharge, with a follow-up appointment scheduled for 08/07/29. He was instructed to seek immediate care should he experience any acute changes in his condition, including increased shortness of breath, chest pain, or significant weight gain.
